audit.summary: Explicit product-of-norms comparison fails finite étale base change; H4 vanishing boundary, missing Postnikov action and disconnected global End1 also corrected. No principal-classification counterexample.
limitations: Limitations: Primary is arXiv v2, not verified publisher-equivalent
Limitations: Later author PDF only locally collated
Limitations: General repair of comparison morphism and all higher coherences not certified
Limitations: No whole-paper or independent acceptance

Separate norms fail base-change naturality — Counterevidence: A standard motivic-K2 comparison may still exist; no counterexample to the principal classification. Later author PDF p19 retains same formula.

Global motivic H4 is not zero — Counterevidence: Correct sheaf cohomology vanishes outside degrees 1,2; this can support a corrected fiber argument after a valid comparison map. Does not itself refute comparison theorem.

Postnikov classification omits the component action — Counterevidence: Forward map-to-extension construction remains valid; torus-connectedness and finite étale coefficients rule out this action in the geometric use. Later author pp12-13 omit old1.2.6-1.2.8.

Global unit endomorphisms require connectedness — Counterevidence: Endomorphism sheaf is constant E; nonempty connected base gives global E. Section6.4 already assumes connectedness. Later author p64 explicitly corrects to sheaf and connectedness.

proposition.claim:
The product of individual coordinate norms defines a presheaf morphism Z_tr(G_m^n) -> K_n.

F=Q perfect, Y=Spec Q[s±1,t±1], Z=Spec Q[u±1,t±1], s=u². Z embeds by x²=s,y=t and is integral finite étale degree 2 over smooth Y.

For connected smooth X/F, H^i_Zar(X,Z(2))=0 for i>=4, attributed to Kahn Theorem 1.6.

F=Q, X=P²_Q smooth connected; section convention is global derived cohomology, not cohomology sheaves.

Maps_E1(H,B^{n+1}A) classifies all two-stage grouplike objects with identified pi0=H and pin=A.

Terminal site, n=1, H=C2, A=C3; convergent 1-truncated Postnikov tower.

Natural E -> End(1) for global sections is an isomorphism without connectedness assumption on S.

S=Spec C disjoint union Spec C, G=G_m, A trivial, mu=0, E a permitted finite Q_l extension.

repair.content:
Use transfer of the product, not product of transfers; in this example Tr{u,t}={-s,t}.

Positive-degree global vanishing starts at i>4; use Kahn Remark 1.5 for sheaf-level fiber calculation.

Require trivial H-action with identification data, or specify action rho and twisted Postnikov class.

End sheaf(1)=E, global End(1)=H0(S,E); impose nonempty connected S for E.
